title: Edge fairness: admission control prevents tenant starvation under overload
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Problem
- With the new gateway admission control + overload protection, we can inadvertently starve low-volume tenants during spikes if we do “first-come/first-serve” or only prioritize high-tier/high-QPS tenants.
- Goal is to preserve tenant isolation and provide predictable access for low-volume tenants, especially for interactive/latency-sensitive workloads, while still protecting the platform under load.

Background / context
- Part of the Reliability Program “Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding”. Admission control is being added at the edge (gateway) to shed early and return consistent overload errors (429/503) with Retry-After.
- During overload, we need fairness between tenants *within a tier* and also ensure that “small” tenants aren’t permanently crowded out by a few high-throughput clients that retry aggressively.

Scope
- Edge fairness only (gateway admission control). Not re-architecting router/runtime scheduler fairness.
- Applies to Hosted API traffic; Dedicated alignment handled separately.

Non-goals
- Replacing quotas/rate limits. This is overload-specific admission behavior.
- Perfect per-request “cost fairness” across heterogeneous prompts (we won’t compute exact token cost at admission time).

Proposed approach
1) Two-stage admission
   - Stage A (coarse): fast reject on global overload conditions (e.g., region is red, breaker open for (model, region, tier)).
   - Stage B (fairness): for requests that pass Stage A, apply a per-tenant fairness gate to avoid single-tenant domination.

2) Fairness mechanism (initial)
   - Per-tenant token bucket (or leaky bucket) rate limiter used only when overload mode is active.
   - Bucket parameters derive from:
     - tier weight (e.g., enterprise > pro > free)
     - per-tenant minimum floor during overload (guaranteed baseline, small but non-zero)
     - optional per-route/model multipliers (streaming vs non-streaming; chat vs embeddings).
   - Key requirement: “low-QPS tenant who sends an occasional request during overload should still have a reasonable chance of admission.”

3) Anti-retry-storm protections
   - Admission decisions must be sticky/cached briefly (per-tenant) to avoid oscillation from immediate client retries.
   - Ensure Retry-After returned and encourage exponential backoff with jitter (handled in ENG-4823/SDK work, but gateway should set consistent Retry-After).

4) Bounded state / cardinality
   - Keep per-tenant state bounded:
     - LRU cache of tenant buckets in gateway
     - separate “anonymous/unknown tenant” bucket for traffic missing auth context
     - hard caps on number of active tenant entries per gateway instance
   - Observability labels must not explode cardinality (tenant_id is NOT a metric label; rely on sampled logs/traces).

Open questions
- What is the right fairness key?
  - API key / org_id / tenant_id? Proposal: org_id (or account_id) + tier + region. Confirm with auth layer.
- How do we handle streaming?
  - Admission occurs before stream starts, but streams hold connections longer. Proposal: apply stricter concurrency gate for streaming routes + smaller token bucket refill under overload.
- How do we handle long prompts?
  - We don’t know exact token count at admission. Proposal: approximate “request cost class” from content-length + route defaults and treat as small/medium/large.

Acceptance criteria
- Under synthetic overload with 2 high-QPS tenants and 100 low-QPS tenants:
  - Low-QPS tenants achieve non-zero success rate (target: at least 95% of low-QPS tenants see at least one successful request per 60s window, assuming they send at least one request per 60s).
  - No tenant can exceed its overload fairness share by more than 2x sustained over a 5-minute window.
- p99 latency does not regress for admitted requests compared to “no fairness gate” overload mode (latency measured only for successful/admitted requests).
- Fairness logic has a safe kill-switch flag (per region) and defaults to current behavior when disabled.
- Metrics added for:
  - admission decisions by tier and route (aggregated)
  - fairness rejections count (aggregated) with reason
  - cache size/evictions for tenant bucket store
  - Retry-After distribution

Implementation notes
- Integrate into the admission control middleware (ENG-4822).
- Reason codes:
  - OVERLOAD_GLOBAL (breaker open)
  - OVERLOAD_FAIRNESS (tenant fairness gate)
  - OVERLOAD_STREAM_CONCURRENCY (if we add this in-gateway)
- Ensure errors map to the standardized overload error taxonomy (ENG-4823).

Testing plan
- Add a perf-canary scenario (step traffic + mixed tenant distribution) as follow-up or coordinate with ENG-4831.
- Unit tests:
  - bucket refill + eviction
  - fairness key derivation
  - expected Retry-After value set
- Load test in staging with replay of traffic distribution from a real spike (use anonymized histogram).

Rollout plan
- Ship behind feature flag: edge_fairness_admission_control
- Canary in us-east for 1–2 models during Phase 3 rollout; monitor fairness reject rate and low-volume tenant success metrics from sampled traces.

References
- Initiative: ENG-4821
- Admission control hook: ENG-4822
- Error semantics: ENG-4823
- Observability: ENG-4829
- Related: PR redwood/pr-18421 (gateway middleware)
comments: 2025-12-12 (Rafael Mendes): Added after SUP-3974 investigation: client retry loops can dominate admission during overload. We need an explicit fairness gate + sticky short-term decisions to reduce starvation + retry feedback loops.

2025-12-16 (Amara Diallo): Drafted design: per-org overload token bucket keyed by (account_id,tier,region). Need confirmation from auth on stable identifier available at gateway for OpenAI-compat endpoints. Also proposing separate small concurrency cap for streaming routes under overload.

2026-01-06 (Allison Grant): Please do not label metrics by tenant/account. Use aggregated counters with tier/route/model/region only; tenant-level analysis should be sampled traces/logs. Add cache eviction metric and a high-watermark gauge.

2026-01-10 (Mina Haddad): Routing will continue to prioritize by tier when breaker is half-open; gateway fairness should be within-tier and not fight routing policies. Suggest: apply fairness after tier admission but before routing calls to reduce control-plane load.

2026-01-15 (Sean Gallagher): Make sure we can explain this externally: “We apply fair-use admission during overload so all tenants have a chance to recover.” Also ensure kill-switch is documented in the oncall runbook.

2026-01-22 (Amara Diallo): Implemented prototype in staging behind flag. Early test: low-volume tenants improved, but streaming concurrency cap was too strict (increased 429 for legitimate interactive clients). Tuning proposal: separate cap for streaming by tier; add jittered Retry-After between 250–750ms for fairness rejects to desynchronize retries.
